New student orientation on campus usually lasts several days. Some schools require all students to attend, while others make it optional for international students, arranging online sessions for them in advance instead.

Orientations are typically scheduled in the week before the start of class for Canadian universities——around late August or early September of the academic year. At the University of Toronto, orientation is mostly optional; for other schools, however, orientation may be mandatory. Therefore, it is important to check your email inbox and factor the orientation date into your travel plan.

Orientations on campus usually last several days. Some schools require all students to attend, while others make it optional for international students, offering online sessions instead. Failure to register for a mandatory orientation may affect your course selection eligibility, so be sure to check the school’s instructions. As for optional orientations, simply sign up before the deadline.

After your enrollment at the university, remember to apply for a dormitory according to the schedule announced by the school and submit the deposit before the deadline. There are multiple dormitories on campus, and the room types may vary slightly. It is recommended to check the school\'s Housing website for floor plans or search for real footage on YouTube.

Most Canadian universities offer on-campus housing to first year students, but the deadline for dorm application may vary, and some schools require an application fee. Make sure to check with your school’s policy for on-campus dorm selection and application.

There are multiple dormitories on campus, and the room types may vary slightly. It is recommended to check the school’s Accommodation website for floor plans or search for room tour footages on YouTube. When filling out the dormitory preferences, you could choose whether to live with friends. If so, make sure to include your friends’ Student ID and ensure that your preference rankings are consistent. The school will make arrangements accordingly, although results are not guaranteed.

To open an account, you will need to bring your passport, visa, I-20, a second form of identification with an English name (Ex. University student ID, English version of the household registration, international driver\'s license), and cash. Common banks for international students include Chase Bank, Bank of America, American Bank, Wells Fargo, Capital One, and Citi Bank.

TD, RBC, CIBC, Scotiabank, and BMO are the most commonly used banks for international students in Canada, all of which offer an opening discount for college students, with TD and RBC being the most common banks across Canada. TD Bank and RBC (Royal Bank of Canada) offer a transaction-free package for up to 25 times per month. CIBC (Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce) and Scotiabank offer an unlimited, transaction-free package. BMO (Bank of Montreal) offers unlimited transactions that require a CA$ 5 fee.

Some of the common banks in the U.K. include HSBC, Barclays, NatWest, Lloyds, TSB, and RBS. Most student accounts function similarly, and no transaction fee is charged between banks. You may visit the bank closest to your school/dormitory to open a bank account.
Each telecom company has different plans, some of which offer student discounts when presented with a university student ID and a passport.

Most international students in Canada use Rogers, Bell, Telus, and Fido. If you live in the suburb, you may use Rogers, Bell, and Telus as they are the leading phone carriers in Canada and cover wider network areas. Fido is quite popular among other phone carriers as it’s the subsidiary company of Rogers’. The above services serve international students as long as the individual provides a valid student ID (or certificates that show proof of enrollment) and a photo ID. Look for discounted plans during back-to-school season.
You might want to travel to other European countries during your study in the U.K., and it is important to find a good network provider with excellent roaming services.

Universities generally release their Academic Calendar for the upcoming academic year before summer break. When scheduling your travels, it is important to consult the school’s official Academic Calendar to avoid missing important dates, such as the start of class and final exams.

Universities typically release their Academic Calendar for the upcoming year near the end of spring or during summer. When scheduling for travel, it is important to consult the official Academic Calendar to avoid missing important dates, such as the start of class and final exams.

In the United States, every university requires all students to provide vaccination records before enrollment. Depending on the regulations of each state, the vaccination dates should be filled out on the form provided by the school. Some schools may require the form to be signed by a physician, and to be uploaded to the school’s system along with the required vaccination record.

There are 3 main components—I-20 , DS-160, and F-1 Visa—and 5 main steps of a student visa application. The 5 Steps to obtain a student visa include: 
	‧Request an I-20 from the university. 
	‧Visit https://www.fmjfee.com to pay 
			US$350 SEVIS fee. 
	‧Visit https://ceac.state.gov/genniv to fill out 
			the DS-160 form. 
	‧Visit the website of your local de facto 
			Embassy of the United States of America to 
			schedule an interview appointment, or to apply 
			for an Interview Waiver program, if 
			applicable. 
	‧Visit your local de facto Embassy of 
			the United States of America for an interview. 
			If you are submitting an Interview Waiver 
			program, mail the requested documents 
			to the designated location.

The Study Permit will remain valid for up to 5 years or until passport expiry (whichever comes first). Check your passport expiration date before applying for a visa. If the remaining validity period of your passport is less than four years, it is recommended that you apply for a new passport first. By doing so, you won’t have to apply for an extension in the future.

Before studying abroad in the U.K., students must obtain a Tier 4 General Student Visa. Once you have decided which university to attend, you must confirm enrollment by providing the school with required documents to meet the offering conditions, and paying the deposit fee. The school will then send you a visa document, namely CAS (Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies). You could apply for a U.K. student visa six months before the start of classes at the earliest. We suggest that you apply for a student visa one month prior to the start of classes at the latest so that you have enough time to prepare for departure.
